title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is sketching a description of the (conjectural) Tannakian category M of motives over a finite field F_p, taken up to isogeny (per the inserted remark 'à isogénie près'). The previous and next pages (numbered 161-162, from Lipman's work on rational double points) are unrelated stray material.

The data considered are:
- M itself, with its grading (weights) and an 'augmentation' (probably the Frobenius / Galois-of-F_p part, cf. G/G° ≅ Ẑ at the bottom);
- the realization fibre functors T_ℓ for ℓ in Specmax(Z);
- functors F_0 (a 'global' fibre functor datum) and F_ℓ.

The motivic Galois group G is described as an extension. Its identity component G° has a kernel H, a group of multiplicative type with H/H° ≅ μ2. The quotients are G°/H ≅ G_m (the weight) and G/G° ≅ Ẑ (Frobenius). Γ is the character group of H, essentially the group of p-Weil numbers.

The category M ∼ the gerbe ℋ of fibre functors. Knowing (M, grading, augmentation, F_0) is equivalent to knowing the class of ℋ as an H-gerbe over Q:
ξ_0 ∈ H²(Q,H) ≅ H²(Q,H°) × H²(Q,μ2).
N.B.: the grading is the homomorphism i*: Γ → Z with i*(λ) = ν ⇔ |λ| = p^{ν/2}, i.e. the weight of a Weil number.

Local analysis:
- For ℓ ≠ p: F_ℓ extends F_0 (up to isomorphism), so the ℓ-adic realization gives a canonical splitting of ℋ over Q_ℓ. Hence (M, grading, augmentation, F_0, F_ℓ for ℓ≠p) is equivalent to a relative class ξ ∈ H²(Q mod T, H), where T = ⊔_{ℓ≠p} Spec Q_ℓ. In particular ξ ∈ H²(Q,H) is locally trivial at all finite ℓ ≠ p.
- For ℓ = p: the crystalline fibre functor T_p (on Dieudonné isocrystals, 'Nisoc(M)°') and F_p are not isomorphic. They differ by a torsor under (G/H) over Q_p, where G/H is the extension of Ẑ by G_m. This is the slope / isocrystal datum at p.

In modern terms this is a programme for describing the motivic gerbe over F_p by a class in H²(Q, P), with P the Weil-number protorus (plus a μ2 component here). The class should be trivial at ℓ ≠ p, governed at p by isocrystals (a G/H-torsor, i.e. a Dieudonné/Kottwitz-type datum), and at ∞ presumably by the sign/μ2 part. This is exactly the shape of the later Langlands–Rapoport 'pseudo-motivic Galois gerbe' and Milne's 'Motives over finite fields'.
errors: The splitting H²(Q,H) ≅ H²(Q,H°) × H²(Q,μ2) presupposes a Galois-equivariant splitting H ≅ H° × μ2 (i.e. the torsion of the character group Γ is a Galois-split Z/2 summand). This is not justified on the page, and in later treatments (Milne, Langlands–Rapoport) the kernel for motives over F̄_p is taken to be a connected protorus.

Passing from local splittings to 'ξ ∈ H²(Q mod T, H)' is correct as relative cohomology. However, the map to H²(Q,H) forgets data (its kernel involves ∏ H¹(Q_ℓ,H)), so 'retenons que ξ splitte aux ℓ≠p' is a weaker statement, as G. himself indicates.

At p, the isocrystal fibre functor naturally lives over the completed maximal unramified extension of Q_p rather than over Q_p, so 'torsion sous (G/H)_{Q_p}' is a simplification of the later B(G)-type (Kottwitz) formalism.
The role of the archimedean place is not treated on this page.

ideas.what: Motives over F_p (up to isogeny) form a Tannakian gerbe banded by a multiplicative-type group H whose characters are Weil numbers, classified by a class in H²(Q,H)
ideas.modern_name: Motivic gerbe over a finite field; Weil-number protorus P
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's ideas as developed in Saavedra Rivano (1972); made precise by Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Milne (1994)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (LNM 265); not in Grothendieck's own publications

ideas.what: Weight grading as the homomorphism Γ → Z, λ ↦ ν with |λ| = p^{ν/2}
ℓ-adic realizations (ℓ≠p) give canonical local trivializations of the motivic gerbe, so its class is a relative class in H²(Q mod ∐_{ℓ≠p} Q_ℓ, H), locally trivial at ℓ≠p
ideas.modern_name: Local triviality of the pseudo-motivic gerbe at ℓ≠p (ζ_ℓ morphisms)

ideas.what: At p, the crystalline (isocrystal) fibre functor differs from the global one by a torsor under G/H, an extension of Ẑ by G_m
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné gerbe / isocrystal gerbe at p (the ζ_p morphism; Kottwitz B(G))

ideas.what: Structure G/G° ≅ Ẑ, G°/H ≅ G_m for the motivic Galois group over F_p
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group over F_p as an extension by the Weil protorus

missed.claim: Grothendieck (in notes plausibly from the late 1960s to 1970s) already formulated the classification of the motivic gerbe over F_p by a cohomology class in H²(Q,H), trivial at all finite ℓ≠p via ℓ-adic realizations and described at p by an isocrystal torsor under (G/H). This is essentially the local–global structure of the Langlands–Rapoport pseudo-motivic gerbe and Milne's description, usually dated to 1987/1994.
missed.quote: Donc ℋ est splittée canoniquement en les ℓ ≠ p [i.e. sur les Q_ℓ] ... ξ ∈ H²(Q mod T, H) où T = ⊔_{ℓ≠p} Spec(Q_ℓ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives priority/historical context for the motivic Galois gerbe used in the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture (proved in cases by Kisin and others). It shows Grothendieck himself framed motives over finite fields as a Galois-cohomological object with local conditions.

missed.claim: The page suggests an explicit μ2 component of the band, H²(Q,H°) × H²(Q,μ2), i.e. a Brauer-class/sign contribution. Later literature eliminates this by working with a connected protorus and modified commutativity constraints. The role of this μ2 factor (likely tied to the sign of the commutativity constraint / real Weil numbers ±p^{1/2}) is left unresolved here.
missed.quote: ξ_0 ∈ H²(Q, H) ≃ H²(Q, H°) × H²(Q, μ_2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could clarify how the non-neutral 'super' or sign issues of motives over F_p are encoded in a Brauer class. This connects to Milne's and Deligne's discussions of the commutativity constraint and the archimedean component of the motivic gerbe.

deep.surprise_reason: The structural picture (Weil-number band, class in H²(Q,P), triviality at ℓ≠p, an isocrystal torsor at p) is known from Langlands–Rapoport and Milne, partly traceable to Grothendieck via Saavedra. Seeing it set up explicitly in Grothendieck's own hand, with relative cohomology H²(Q mod T, H) and the G/H-torsor at p, is a notable unpublished precursor, but not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'la fonction F_ℓ quotientée (à isom. près) la fonction F_0' is more plausibly 'la fonction F_ℓ prolonge (à isom. près) la fonction F_0'.
In the bottom insertion, 'le changement de G/G° ≃ Ẑ par G°/H ≃ G_m' should likely read 'l'extension de G/G° ≃ Ẑ par G°/H ≃ G_m'.
'Donc[?] :' at the start of the second paragraph may be 'On en tire :' or similar.
'Nisoc(M)°' refers to the (neutral component of the) category of isocrystals attached to M; T_p is the crystalline realization functor on it.
